title: Magnetic Force on a Moving Charge in about 10 minutes

intro.heading: One field, one moving charge, one sideways push
lines: A charged particle moving through a magnetic field feels a push. This push is called the magnetic force.
The push is sideways — always at a right angle to the velocity. It turns the particle instead of speeding it up.
The size of the force is F = qvB sin θ, where θ is the angle between the velocity and the field.
Old television picture tubes steered their electron beam with exactly this force. Let us see it.

what_changes.you_change: Angle θ between v and B
what_changes.you_see: The path changes shape: straight line, then helix, then circle
The force flips to the opposite side

readings.label: angle θ between v and B
readings.name: theta_slider

missions.instruction: Watch the proton. Its velocity points along the blue field arrows, the angle is zero, and the force readout stays at zero. No force — it moves in a straight line.
Drag the angle slider to 30 degrees or more. The moment the velocity tilts away from the field, a force appears and the path starts to bend.
missions.hint: The angle slider is in the panel at the top right of the simulation.

missions.instruction: Now the velocity is fully across the field and the path is a circle. Raise the speed to 3 or more. Watch the circle grow.
missions.hint: The speed slider is marked |v| in the top-right panel.

missions.instruction: Now raise the field B to 30 mT or more. The circle pulls tighter — and check the small pale markers on the path: still equally spaced. The speed never changes.
missions.hint: The field slider is marked B in the top-right panel.

missions.instruction: This is the right-hand rule: fingers along v, curl toward B, thumb gives F. Now click the +e badge to flip the charge to negative, and watch the force arrow flip to the opposite side.
missions.hint: The +e badge is at the top of the panel on the right. Click it once.

missions.instruction: The angle is 45 degrees and the path is a helix — part of v circles, part drifts along the field. Drag the angle down to 20 degrees or less and watch the helix stretch out toward a straight line.
missions.hint: Drag the angle slider toward zero and watch the path change shape.

key_ideas: The magnetic force is zero when the velocity is along the field, and largest when it is across the field.
The force is always at a right angle to the velocity, so it turns the particle but never changes its speed.
Only the part of v across the field makes the circle. The part along the field drifts freely — together they make a helix.

formula.reading: Force equals charge times speed times field strength times the sine of the angle between v and B.

common_mistake.wrong: A stronger magnetic field makes the particle go faster.
common_mistake.right: The magnetic force never changes the speed. A stronger field only bends the path into a tighter circle.

ql_no_work.replay_prompt: Watch the small pale markers on the circle — they stay equally spaced the whole time, so the speed never changes.

ql_flip_sign.replay_prompt: Click the +e badge to flip the charge, and watch the force arrow jump to the opposite side.

welcome: Hi! I am Vidi, your guide for this lesson.
One proton, one magnetic field, and one rule that runs everything from old TV tubes to particle accelerators. Do each small step with me — and ask me anything, any time, in the box below.

celebrations.m1: You saw it! The velocity points along the field, the angle is zero, and the force readout stays at zero. No force — a straight line.
celebrations.m2: There it is! The moment v tilts away from B, a force appears and the path starts to bend.
celebrations.m3: Nice! A faster proton makes a bigger circle. The radius grows with speed: r = mv/qB.
celebrations.m4: You did it! A stronger field pulls the circle tighter. And the pale markers stayed equally spaced — the speed never changed.
celebrations.m5: Exactly! Negative charge, opposite force. Same rule, opposite thumb.
celebrations.m6: You found it! As the angle shrinks, more of the velocity drifts along the field and the helix stretches out. At zero it becomes a straight line again.

tutor.quiz_intro: Now let us check what you learned. 5 questions. You have seen every answer happen on the screen.
tutor.summary_line: Great work today. Every step you took and every question you asked is saved, so you can pick up where you left off.
